project.name: PoshanAI
project.tagline: Nutrition awareness and practical meal planning using familiar Indian foods.
project.purpose: A web application for account-based nutrition tracking, Indian food lookup, report OCR, lifestyle recommendations, and meal-plan suggestions.
audience: People seeking practical Indian meal suggestions
People reviewing lab-report values with educational context
project.medicalBoundary: The app provides nutrition awareness and suggestions. It does not diagnose, treat, or replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional.
project.implementationReality: The repository contains an active JavaScript MERN application. The reserved ai-service directory is not an active Python service. AI text parsing and meal-plan calls run from the Express backend through an OpenAI-compatible OmniRoute endpoint.

frontend.forms: React Hook Form, Zod, and Joi validation on the server
frontend.state: React Context for session/theme; Redux Toolkit for reports, meal plans, food logs, and user state
frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS plus project CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, and selected Three.js scenes

backend.authentication: JWT access tokens and rotating HTTP-only refresh-token cookies
backend.storage: Local filesystem or AWS S3 adapter

ai.providerPath: OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint configured by OMNIROUTE_URL.
ai.secretSetting: OMNIROUTE_API_KEY is optional and remains server-side.
ai.dataGrounding: Bundled IFCT-derived food records are used to search food names and calculate nutrient values. The model does not own the nutrition arithmetic for meal plans.
ai.notImplemented: No active Python OCR/RAG microservice is present.

rules: Never store secrets in tracked JSON, source, frontend VITE variables, screenshots, or logs.
JWT access and refresh secrets must be strong, at least 32 characters in production, and distinct when separately configured.
Production requires Redis for distributed rate limits and background jobs; local development can run without it.
Production S3 mode requires S3_BUCKET and S3_REGION; access key and secret must be configured together or use workload credentials.
MONGODB_TLS is validated; production remote MongoDB requires TLS.

prefixes.note: app.js mounts most routers under both API prefixes. Check app.js for exact mounts before adding another route.

routes.notes: Password login uses email/password. Email verification is not a login gate. TOTP two-factor authentication is a separate feature. Access JWTs are short-lived; refresh tokens are rotated and stored hashed.
Supported purposes are login and reset-password. Email delivery uses configured Gmail SMTP. Resend email verification is not in the MVP.

POST /api/user/profile is present in the current uncommitted snapshot. It updates the authenticated user's profile and does not accept identity from the body. Password is stored as passwordHash, not plaintext.
Onboarding validates consent and lifestyle fields, persists the caller's data, and controls completion gating.
Uploads are restricted to PDF/JPEG/PNG, signature-checked, capped at 10 MB, stored privately, and ownership checked.
Generation requires an owned completed report; requests are queued when Redis is available and validated before persistence.
Basic IFCT-backed plan flow is distinct from report-based mealplans.

routes.access: mostly bearer; food catalog and supplement catalog are public read-only
routes.notes: There are legacy and newer logging route groups. Inspect the frontend API client to see which is used by each screen. Nutrients are calculated server-side from the IFCT data.

routes.access: directory read is public; booking actions require bearer
routes.notes: Booking and appointment models coexist; inspect the current controller/service before changing their lifecycle.
User notifications include scheduled water, meal-log, and retest reminders when worker/scheduler support is available.

sessionFlow: AuthContext calls the feature methods in src/api/authApi.js.
The Axios client attaches the in-memory access token and handles refresh-cookie session renewal.
Registration/login responses populate the user and access-token state; refresh tokens are HTTP-only cookies.
ProtectedRoute blocks unauthenticated navigation and onboarding completion gates downstream app routes.
frontend.designNotes: The UI uses a forest/sage/paper palette, serif display typography, reusable accessible controls, responsive layouts, and motion/3D elements. Prefer existing components and honor reduced-motion behavior when editing UI.

dataModels.User: Auth identity, bcrypt passwordHash, verified-status compatibility flag, role, profile subdocument, consent, onboarding state, TOTP data, refresh-session hashes, account status, and upload quotas. Sensitive TOTP/refresh/password paths are selectively hidden. The current worktree adds monthlyFoodBudget to the profile subdocument.
dataModels.LifestyleProfile: Separate questionnaire model with userId, demographics, dietType, meals/day, typicalDiet, dailyDietDescription, sleep, sun exposure, activity, habits, symptoms, consent; unique userId index.
dataModels.Report: Owned uploaded file metadata, OCR/review status, raw OCR text, extracted biomarkers, micronutrient intake, processing and retention/retest timestamps; raw OCR is encrypted.
dataModels.MealPlan: Report-linked, owned multi-day plan with preferences, household diet, deficiencies, meals/items, IFCT codes, portions, nutrient targets, cooking instructions, status, model/source metadata, and mandatory disclaimer.
dataModels.DietPlan: Separate basic/personalized plan model with calorie/macro targets, profile snapshot, goal, meals and IFCT item references.
dataModels.FoodLog and DailyLog: Owned dated food entries. FoodLog encrypts item details; DailyLog stores meals and calculated nutrients with a unique user/date index.
dataModels.SupplementLog: Owned dated supplement entries and micronutrient amounts.
dataModels.Otp: Email, purpose (login/reset-password only), bcrypt OTP hash, attempts, and expiry TTL index.
dataModels.Notification: User-targeted reminder/notification content, optional report/dedupe keys, read state and optional emailSentAt compatibility field.
dataModels.Expert and ExpertAppointment: Expert directory and scheduled appointment records.
dataModels.Booking: Current worktree adds user/expert/date/timeSlot/status booking data and indexes preventing simultaneous active bookings for a slot.
dataModels.AuditLog: User/action/time, request metadata and event metadata for audit records.

authentication: Register validates name/email/password/consent, hashes password with bcrypt, creates a session, and returns an access JWT plus refresh cookie.
Password login looks up by normalized email, checks bcrypt password, then issues a session. Email verification is not a login gate in the MVP.
If twoFactorEnabled is true, login returns a separate TOTP challenge; this is not Resend email verification.
Refresh validates and rotates the refresh token; only a SHA-256 token hash is stored. Logout revokes a session; logout-all revokes all sessions.
OTP routes remain for code-based sign-in and password reset. Email verification OTP purpose was removed.
onboardingAndProfile: Register creates the account; the authenticated user completes consent-first lifestyle onboarding.
Lifestyle data is associated with the caller identity, never a body-supplied userId.
Profile supports GET/PATCH /api/users/me. The current uncommitted profile work adds POST /api/user/profile, maps dietaryPreference to existing dietType, and stores monthlyFoodBudget under profile.
Profile changes do not accept or persist plaintext passwords. Password changes use dedicated auth/reset flows.
reportOcr: Authenticated report upload accepts one PDF/JPEG/PNG with magic-byte checking, a 10 MB request cap, private storage and per-user quotas.
When Redis is available, BullMQ queues OCR; otherwise local development processes OCR synchronously with a timeout.
Tesseract uses English and Hindi trained data; PDF pages are rendered to images with resource caps.
Report parser extracts supported biomarkers and values; review endpoints let the user confirm or correct extraction.
Report reads/deletes and all stored-file operations are ownership checked.
householdMealPlanning: Meal-plan generation requires the authenticated user's OCR-completed report and validated diet/allergy/region/activity preferences.
IFCT loader reads bundled records and normalizes selected names to household labels.
A household whitelist limits normal retrieval to familiar Indian foods; explicit food requests may add eligible requested records, with permanent exclusions enforced for barley.
Prompt requires familiar staples, respects the user's typical diet, uses realistic cooking, and tells the model to select foods and portions only.
Backend validates returned IFCT codes and portion bounds, looks up nutrient values, calculates macros from IFCT, and applies the medical disclaimer before persistence.
Redis-enabled deployments can queue plan generation; status endpoints expose job progress.
dailyNutrition: Food search returns IFCT entries and serving metadata.
Food and supplement logging is authenticated. Server resolves food codes/serving units, computes nutrient totals, and persists dated user entries.
Dashboard and tracker screens display calorie/macronutrient and micronutrient summaries against project reference values.
AI food parsing produces a preview; the user confirms before persistence.
notificationsAndRetention: Notification endpoints list/read only the authenticated user's notifications.
Optional Redis workers/schedulers process notification and retention/retest jobs.
Retest reminders are in-app in the current MVP; email verification/Resend is future scope.

expectedFoodPolicy: Prefer everyday affordable Indian foods: roti, rice, poha, oats when present in IFCT candidates, potato, dal, rajma, chole, dahi, paneer, eggs, chicken, fish, soya chunks, chana and common vegetables.
Preserve familiar staples from typicalDiet/householdDiet and adjust portions/add suitable protein rather than replacing the user's normal meals.
Use boiling, pressure cooking, steaming, or minimal-oil tadka; do not recommend deep frying.
Do not use amaranth, agathi, ragi, or quinoa unless explicitly requested and present in the allowed records. Barley is forbidden.
Only use food code/name pairs passed from the backend; respect dietary preference and allergen filters.
nutritionAiRules.nutrientAuthority: The IFCT database and backend are authoritative for nutrition values. The model chooses food records and portions; backend code calculates calories, protein, carbohydrate, fat, and available micronutrients. Do not trust model-invented macro fields.
nutritionAiRules.caveat: The AI gateway must be configured and reachable. Model output is untrusted until schema/code/portion validation succeeds.

securityAndPrivacy: Use verifyToken on every user-scoped API route; use requireRole for admin-only routes.
Derive user ownership from req.user, not request-body userId.
Validate POST/PATCH inputs with Joi and strip or reject unknown fields.
Never store raw passwords; use bcrypt passwordHash and verifyPassword().
Access tokens use HS256; refresh tokens are HTTP-only, SameSite strict cookies and are rotated/revoked server-side.
Use ipKeyGenerator(req.ip) in custom express-rate-limit keys to support IPv6 correctly.
Trust only configured reverse-proxy hops; do not blindly trust X-Forwarded-For.
Helmet, restricted credentialed CORS, JSON size limits, Mongo operator sanitization, and API limits are applied in app.js.
Uploads must pass allowed MIME and magic-byte checks, have random server filenames, remain private, and be cleaned up safely.
Health and audit logs must not reveal secrets, tokens, PII, or raw health data.

testsAndQuality.guidance: Use focused tests around touched behavior, then the broader suite when appropriate. Never claim a suite passed unless it was run and its output observed.

knownCaveats: README and older architecture documents may lag source. This guide is a dated map; verify route/model behavior in source before relying on it.
There are two related but distinct plan systems: report-linked mealplans and basic diet-plans.
There are overlapping legacy log and daily-log API route groups; use the established frontend API module for the screen being changed.
Compose backend ports and direct local ports differ by design: direct backend defaults to 5000; Compose commonly maps API to 4000 and frontend to 8080.
The report-based AI mealplan path and the basic diet plan path have different request/response models; do not merge them casually.
Lifestyle recommendation content depends on reviewed data in data/testRules.json and may be empty. Never invent clinical recommendations to fill it.
